description: The lion is a large felid native to Africa and India. Muscular and broad-chested with a tufted tail, adult males possess a magnificent dark mane. It is the only truly social wild cat, living in structured family prides.
distinguishing_characteristics: Prominent mane in adult males
Tawny yellow-gold unspotted coat in adults
Black brush tuft at tail tip
Social pride structure of related females and a coalition of males
geographic_range: Sub-Saharan Africa; Gir National Park in Gujarat, Western India
diet: Apex obligate carnivore; primarily large ungulates (wildebeest, zebras, buffalo)
behavior: Social pride living; mostly nocturnal and crepuscular hunting; roaring audible up to 8 km.
image_attribution: Photo: Giles Laurent / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

similar_species.differentiator: Cougars have a smaller, sleeker head, no mane, white muzzle ring, and purr rather than roar.

description: The tiger is the largest living cat species. Recognizable for its dark vertical stripes on reddish-orange fur with white underbellies. Solitary apex predators with an affinity for water and swimming.
distinguishing_characteristics: Distinctive vertical black stripes unique to every individual
Reddish-orange coat with white ventral coloration
Prominent white spot ('ocellus') on the back of each ear
Superior swimming and aquatic ambush capabilities
size_and_weight: Total length: up to 310 cm; Weight: 90-300 kg depending on subspecies
geographic_range: South Asia, Southeast Asia, and the Russian Far East
diet: Large ungulates including deer (sambar, chital), wild boar, and wild cattle
behavior: Solitary and territorial; patrol large home ranges; frequently bathes in rivers.
image_attribution: Photo: Charles J. Sharp / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

description: The jaguar is the only extant Panthera species native to the Americas. Muscular and stocky, it possesses the most crushing bite force relative to body size of all cats, puncturing turtle carapaces with ease.
distinguishing_characteristics: Large rosette patterns containing central black spots
Exceptionally compact, muscular build with broad head and thick jaw
Direct cranial bite strategy piercing temporal skull bones
Strong affinity for swimming in rivers and swamps
size_and_weight: Head-body: 112-185 cm; Weight: 56-96 kg (exceptional males exceed 140 kg)
geographic_range: Southwestern US borderlands through Central America to the Pantanal and Amazon
diet: Broad generalist: caiman, capybaras, tapirs, turtles, and peccaries
behavior: Solitary apex predator; stalk-and-ambush hunter; adept swimmer.
image_attribution: Photo: USFWS / Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)

similar_species.differentiator: Leopard rosettes lack interior black spots and leopards have longer, leaner frames.

description: The leopard is famous for its supreme agility, stealth, and arboreal strength. It hoists carcasses heavier than its own body high into tree branches to protect them from hyenas and lions.
distinguishing_characteristics: Dense rosettes with hollow, spot-free centers
Slender athletic build with long balancing tail (60-100 cm)
Master of climbing; rests and caches food aloft
Frequent melanistic ('black panther') morphs in humid tropical zones
geographic_range: Sub-Saharan Africa, Middle East, Central Asia, India, and China
diet: Opportunistic: antelopes, deer, baboons, and wild pigs
behavior: Nocturnal and solitary; caches prey in tree forks.
image_attribution: Photo: Sumeet Moghe / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

similar_species.differentiator: Cheetahs have solid round spots, facial tear marks, and tall slender builds.

description: The 'Ghost of the Mountains' roams the high peaks of Central Asia. Perfectly adapted to alpine conditions with thick smoky fur, broad snowshoe paws, and an enormous tail wrapped around its face for warmth.
distinguishing_characteristics: Thick smoky-grey fur with muted black rosettes
Exceptionally long, plush tail (80-105 cm) used as balance and muffler
Fur-covered footpads providing snow traction
Large nasal cavity warming frigid thin air before lung entry
geographic_range: High mountains of Central and South Asia (Himalayas, Tien Shan, Altai)
diet: Mountain ungulates (blue sheep/bharal, ibex, markhor) and marmots
behavior: Solitary cliff stalker; leaps up to 15 meters; non-roaring vocal anatomy.
image_attribution: Photo: Irbis1983 / Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)

description: A canopy specialist of Southeast Asian rainforests. It has the longest canines in proportion to skull size of any living carnivore and can climb down tree trunks headfirst like a squirrel.
distinguishing_characteristics: Enormous canine teeth relative to head size (up to 4 cm)
Large cloud-shaped irregular dark blotches
Reversible ankle joints allowing head-first vertical descent
Extremely long balancing tail and wide stabilizing paws
geographic_range: Southeast Asia, southern China, eastern Himalayas
diet: Primates (gibbons, macaques), deer, and wild pigs
behavior: Arboreal hunter; drops from branches onto terrestrial prey; nocturnal.
image_attribution: Photo: Rushenb / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

description: Native to Borneo and Sumatra, genetically distinct from the mainland clouded leopard. It features smaller, darker cloud markings with distinctive central spots inside the clouds.
distinguishing_characteristics: Darker overall pelage with smaller cloud blotches containing inner spots
Proportionately huge canines and muscular arboreal limbs
Heavy double dorsal stripe running along back
Strictly restricted to the Sunda islands of Borneo and Sumatra
geographic_range: Islands of Borneo and Sumatra (Indonesia, Malaysia, Brunei)
diet: Sambar deer, mouse deer, bearded pigs, proboscis monkeys
behavior: Canopy predator; highly elusive; threatened by palm oil deforestation.
image_attribution: Photo: www.photosbypaulo.com / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)

similar_species.differentiator: Mainland clouded leopards are lighter yellow-tawny with larger, cleaner cloud markings.

description: A medium-sized forest cat of Southeast Asia exhibiting polymorphic coloration ranging from golden-red and dark brown to spotted and melanistic phases. Known for conspicuous white facial lines.
distinguishing_characteristics: Conspicuous white lines flanked by dark brown stripes extending from inner eye corners upward
Tail tip underside is conspicuously whitish and carried curled upward
Solid golden, chestnut, or grey coat phase ('golden cat')
Powerful stocky limbs adapted to mountain forests
geographic_range: Northeast India, Bhutan, Southeast Asia, southern China, Sumatra
diet: Muntjacs (barking deer), wild pigs, mouse deer, and ground birds
behavior: Both terrestrial and arboreal hunter; solitary; marks trails with urine and scent.
image_attribution: Photo: Karen Stout / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)

conservation_title: Endangered (One of the world's most elusive cats)
description: Endemic exclusively to the island of Borneo. Characterized by its chestnut-red or slate-grey coat, long tapering tail with a pale underside, and rounded head with short ears.
distinguishing_characteristics: Endemic strictly to Borneo island
Long tail tapering toward tip with distinctive white ventral line
Small rounded ears set low on the skull
Extremely low camera-trap detection rates; fewer than 2,500 remain
size_and_weight: Head-body: 53-67 cm; Tail: 32-39 cm; Weight: 3-4 kg
geographic_range: Endemic to the island of Borneo (Indonesia & Malaysia)
diet: Small forest rodents, birds, and lizards
behavior: Extremely secretive forest specialist; primarily nocturnal; severely threatened by logging.
image_attribution: Photo: Jim Sanderson derivative work: Abujoy / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)

description: The marbled cat looks like a miniature clouded leopard, with marbled blotches and an extraordinarily long, bushy tail longer than its head-body length used to balance aloft in canopy vines.
distinguishing_characteristics: Bushy tail exceeding the length of its head and body (up to 55 cm)
Irregular clouded marbled patches with thick dark borders
Flexible limbs with broad paws designed for canopy locomotion
Miniature build weighing only 2-5 kg
size_and_weight: Head-body: 45-62 cm; Tail: 35-55 cm; Weight: 2-5 kg
geographic_range: Eastern Himalayas through Southeast Asia, Sumatra, and Borneo
diet: Arboreal rodents, squirrels, tree birds, and bats
behavior: Almost exclusively arboreal and crepuscular; acrobatic forest canopy dweller.
image_attribution: Photo: Johan Embréus (Embreus ) / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 3.0)

similar_species.differentiator: Clouded leopards are four times heavier with massive canines and shorter relative tails.

description: Characterized by long black ear tufts and an unspotted tawny-red coat. Known for its acrobatic vertical jumps snatching birds out of mid-air up to 3 meters above the ground.
distinguishing_characteristics: Extremely long black ear tufts exceeding 4.5 cm
Uniform reddish-tawny coat without torso spotting
20 individual ear muscles directing auditory radar
Astounding aerial leaping ability catching flying gamebirds
geographic_range: Africa, Middle East, Central Asia, and northwestern India
diet: Guineafowl, francolins, hares, rodents, and small antelopes
behavior: Nocturnal and solitary; marks territory with scent and claw markings.
image_attribution: Photo: Derek Keats / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)

similar_species.differentiator: Servals are heavily spotted with round dish-like ears; caracals are unspotted with tufted ears.

description: Endemic to the equatorial rainforests of Central and West Africa. Exhibiting rich golden-red to slate-grey coloration, it is twice the size of a domestic cat and closely related to the caracal.
distinguishing_characteristics: Rounded head with small ears lacking long caracal-style tufts
Coat varies from bright reddish-gold to silver-grey or chocolate
Variable spotting, often prominent on belly and inner legs
Specialized inhabitant of the Congo Basin tropical forests
geographic_range: Equatorial rainforest belt of Central and West Africa (Congo Basin)
diet: Forest duikers, giant pouched rats, monkeys, and tree pangolins
behavior: Secretive terrestrial stalker; rarely observed directly; threatened by bushmeat hunting.
image_attribution: Photo: Greco & Rovero / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 4.0)

description: Has the longest legs and biggest ears relative to body size of any cat. These acoustic radar adaptations allow it to pinpoint burrowing rodents beneath savanna reeds and pounce in high parabolic arcs.
distinguishing_characteristics: Disproportionately long, slender stilting legs
Enormous upright oval ears set closely together
Golden coat with bold black spots merging into neck bars
High arching vertical pounce with >50% hunting success
size_and_weight: Head-body: 59-100 cm; Shoulder height: 54-62 cm; Weight: 7-18 kg
geographic_range: Sub-Saharan Africa, centered on well-watered savanna wetlands
diet: Small rodents (vlei rats), birds, frogs, and lizards
behavior: Auditory hunter; stalks through tall grass; solitary.
image_attribution: Photo: Diego Delso / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

similar_species.differentiator: Caracals have pointed tufted ears and uniform unspotted red coats.

description: Medium-sized neotropical spotted cat ranging from southern Texas to northern Argentina. Marked with longitudinal chains of elongated rosettes and parallel cheek stripes.
distinguishing_characteristics: Chains of dark-bordered elongated spots running in lines down the body
Prominent white spot ('ocellus') on back of each ear
Muscular body weighing 8-16 kg
Reversible ankle joints for tree climbing
geographic_range: Southern Texas through Central America to Northern Argentina
diet: Opossums, armadillos, rodents, birds, and iguanas
behavior: Nocturnal and solitary; maintains scent-sprayed pathways.
image_attribution: Photo: Giles Laurent / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

similar_species.differentiator: Margays are half the size with proportionally giant eyes and longer tails.

description: The supreme acrobat of the cat family. Its hind ankles can rotate 180 degrees, allowing it to run vertically down tree trunks headfirst and hang from branches by a single foot.
distinguishing_characteristics: Enormous nocturnal eyes adapted for rainforest canopy depth perception
Hind ankles rotate 180° inward for acrobatic tree navigation
Extremely long tail (70% of head-body length) for balance
Vocal mimicry of prey species (e.g. pied tamarin infants)
size_and_weight: Head-body: 48-79 cm; Tail: 33-51 cm; Weight: 2.6-4 kg
geographic_range: Mexico through Central America to northern Argentina and Uruguay
diet: Canopy rodents, squirrels, tree frogs, fruit, and small birds
behavior: Strictly arboreal and nocturnal; lives life in high canopy branches.
image_attribution: Photo: Supreet Sahoo / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

similar_species.differentiator: Ocelots are much heavier with smaller relative eye diameters.

description: One of the rarest, most endangered felids in existence. Surviving only on barren, freezing Andean slopes above 3,500 meters, it preys almost exclusively on mountain viscachas.
distinguishing_characteristics: Thick cylindrical tail with 6-9 dark brown rings, almost as long as body
Ash-grey plush coat with orange-brown vertical flank bars
Strictly restricted to high rocky scree in the Andes (>3,500 m)
Specialized predator of chinchillas and mountain viscachas
size_and_weight: Head-body: 57-64 cm; Tail: 41-48 cm; Weight: 4-5 kg
geographic_range: High Andes of Peru, Bolivia, northern Chile, and northwest Argentina
diet: Mountain viscachas (Lagidium viscacia) and high-elevation rodents
behavior: Solitary scree climber; counterbalances rapid leaps with thick tail.
image_attribution: Photo: Jim Sanderson / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)

description: The smallest wild cat in the Americas, weighing only 1.5-3 kg. Native to the temperate Valdivian rainforests of Chile and adjacent Argentina, it has a tiny face, bushy ringed tail, and black spots.
distinguishing_characteristics: Smallest felid in the Western Hemisphere (1.5-3 kg)
Brownish-yellow coat densely covered in small round black spots
Bushy tail with 10-12 dark rings
High rate of melanism (pure black morphs common)
geographic_range: Central and southern Chile, western border of Argentina
diet: Small forest rodents, thrushes, chucao tapaculos, lizards
behavior: Agile climber; nests in tree hollows; threatened by forest fragmentation.
image_attribution: Photo: Mauro Tammone / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 3.0)

description: Native to the southern half of South America. About the size of a domestic cat, covered in countless small black spots, and renowned for frequently standing upright on its hind legs to survey surroundings.
distinguishing_characteristics: Regularly stands upright on hind legs ('tripod stance') to peer over tall grass
Numerous small, clearly separated black spots over silvery-ochre coat
Excellent swimmer that readily enters wetlands for fish and frogs
Dark cheek lines and prominent white ear patches
geographic_range: Pampas and Gran Chaco of Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay
diet: Hares, rodents, marsh birds, fish, and frogs
behavior: Solitary and nocturnal; uses tree crotches as latrines and resting sites.
image_attribution: Photo: Daf-de / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.5)

description: The largest of the four lynx species and third largest European predator. Characterized by long black ear tufts, flared facial ruff, powerful hindquarters, and huge snowshoe paws.
distinguishing_characteristics: Prominent 4 cm black ear tufts acting as acoustic aids
Short bobbed tail ending in a completely black tip
Wide facial ruff framing the jaw
Furred, webbed paws distributing weight across deep winter snow
geographic_range: Northern and Eastern Europe, Siberia, and Central Asia
diet: Medium-sized ungulates (roe deer, chamois) and mountain hares
behavior: Solitary stalker; exceptional sight and hearing; patrols vast home ranges.
image_attribution: Photo: Aconcagua / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)

similar_species.differentiator: Canada lynx are smaller (8-14 kg) with silver coats and even bigger snowshoe paws.

description: Adaptable North American predator ranging from southern Canada to central Mexico. Named for its stubby bobbed tail, which uniquely features a bright white underside at the tip.
distinguishing_characteristics: Tail tip is black on dorsal side but clear bright white underneath
Reddish-brown to grey-brown pelage with dark bar markings on forelimbs
Moderate black ear tufts shorter than Canadian lynx
White eye circles and white ear spots
geographic_range: North America from southern Canada throughout the US to central Mexico
diet: Cottontail rabbits, hares, rodents, birds, and young ungulates
behavior: Crepuscular and territorial; agile climber and swimmer.
image_attribution: Photo: Becker1999 (Paul and Cathy) / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)

similar_species.differentiator: Canada lynx tails are solid black all around the tip with no white underside.

description: Specialized boreal hunter whose population numbers fluctuate in tandem with the 10-year abundance cycle of snowshoe hares. Has enormous snowshoe paws with low foot loading.
distinguishing_characteristics: Tail tip is entirely black on all sides
Huge fur-padded paws creating low pressure on powder snow
Very long ear tufts (>3.5 cm) and flared beard ruff
Silvery-grey thick winter fur with faint markings
geographic_range: Boreal forests of Canada and Alaska, northern tier of US states
diet: Snowshoe hares (75-97% of diet), grouse, and red squirrels
behavior: Crepuscular and nocturnal; travels silently through deep snow.
image_attribution: Photo: Michael Zahra / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)

description: The world's most threatened felid in 2002, now recovering in Spain and Portugal thanks to historic reintroduction initiatives. Features heavy leopard-like spots and a rabbit-dependent diet.
distinguishing_characteristics: Intensely spotted coat with crisp, dark, leopard-like markings
Long pointed ear tufts and pronounced dual-pointed facial beard
Strict dietary dependence on European wild rabbits (>80%)
Endemic to Mediterranean maquis scrub of Spain and Portugal
geographic_range: Iberian Peninsula (Andalusia, Castilla-La Mancha, Extremadura, Alentejo)
diet: European wild rabbits (Oryctolagus cunicuniculus)
behavior: Solitary territorial predator; European rewilding flagship.
image_attribution: Photo: Diego Delso / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

description: The fastest terrestrial mammal, capable of bursts up to 112 km/h (70 mph). Evolutionarily specialized with semi-retractile claws for traction, deep chest, and dark facial tear lines.
distinguishing_characteristics: Black tear stripes from eye corners to mouth to reduce solar glare
Solid small round black spots over golden fur
Semi-retractile claws functioning like track sprint spikes
Deep chest and flexible spine enabling massive sprinting strides
geographic_range: Eastern and Southern Africa; relict Asiatic cheetah population in Iran
diet: Medium ungulates (Thomson's gazelle, impala, springbok) and hares
behavior: Diurnal hunter avoiding larger nocturnal carnivores; high-speed sprint chase.
image_attribution: Photo: AfricanConservation / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

similar_species.differentiator: Leopards are stocky with rosettes; cheetahs have solid dots and tear stripes.

description: Holds the record for the broadest latitudinal range of any native terrestrial mammal in the Western Hemisphere, stretching from northern Yukon to Patagonia. A large, solitary purring cat.
distinguishing_characteristics: Tawny-beige unspotted coat with white muzzle ring and black whisker spots
Cylindrical tail with prominent dark black tip
Massive hind legs powering vertical leaps of up to 5.5 meters
Purring felid; lacks hyoid elasticity required to roar
geographic_range: Western Canada and US through Central and South America to Tierra del Fuego
diet: Deer (mule deer, white-tailed deer), elk, bighorn sheep, and smaller mammals
behavior: Solitary ambush hunter; caches kills under brush and snow.
image_attribution: Photo: National Park Service / Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)

similar_species.differentiator: Lions have much larger skulls, male manes, pride lifestyle, and roar.

description: An unusual neotropical cat with an otter-like body, short limbs, small flattened head, and unspotted coat occurring in grey and red color morphs. Predominantly active by day.
distinguishing_characteristics: Otter-like low elongated silhouette with short legs and long tail
Unspotted coat in two morphs: dark charcoal-grey and bright red-chestnut
Strictly diurnal (daytime hunter)
Unusual vocal repertoire of 13 vocalizations including bird-like chirps
geographic_range: Central America and South America to central Argentina
diet: Ground birds (chachalacas), rodents, snakes, and lizards
behavior: Diurnal ground stalker; moves through dense brush; highly vocal.
image_attribution: Photo: Vassil / Wikimedia Commons (CC0)

description: Adapted to the high-altitude, freezing steppes of Central Asia. Possesses the densest fur of any felid, low-set ears allowing it to peer over rock edges without being seen, and unique round pupils.
distinguishing_characteristics: Low-set, widely spaced rounded ears on the sides of the flat head
Circular pupils that contract into round dots rather than vertical slits
Plush, frosted silvery coat protecting against subzero temperatures
Short, heavily furred black-tipped tail
geographic_range: Central Asian steppes (Mongolia, Tibetan Plateau, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan)
diet: Pikas, voles, small ground birds, and insects
behavior: Ambush hunter in rocky outcrops; low profile stalking; solitary.
image_attribution: Photo: Sander van der Wel / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)

description: Small spotted wild cat widespread across South, Southeast, and East Asia. Wild progenitor of the modern domestic Bengal cat breed. An agile climber and capable swimmer.
distinguishing_characteristics: Two conspicuous dark facial stripes running up from forehead to nape
Yellow-ochre coat patterned with black rosettes and spots
White muzzle, chin, and throat
Adept swimmer and agile climber
geographic_range: Widespread across Asia from India to China, Korea, and Russian Far East
diet: Murid rodents, bats, small birds, reptiles, and amphibians
behavior: Nocturnal and solitary; often frequents oil palm and agricultural boundaries.
image_attribution: Photo: Abujoy / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)

description: A semiaquatic wetland specialist in South and Southeast Asia. Features partially webbed front paws, water-resistant double coat, and a habit of diving underwater to catch fish.
distinguishing_characteristics: Partially webbed front paws powering aquatic propulsion
Dense water-resistant undercoat preventing skin saturation
Strong rudder-like muscular tail
Taps water surfaces to mimic insects and draw fish within strike reach
geographic_range: Disjunct wetlands of South and Southeast Asia (India, Sri Lanka, Thailand)
diet: Fish (>75% of diet), crabs, water snakes, mollusks, and frogs
behavior: Semiaquatic hunter; swims long distances; predominantly nocturnal.
image_attribution: Photo: Kelinahandbasket / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)

description: An extreme semiaquatic specialist of Sundaland peat swamps. Has an elongated skull with flattened forehead, close-set eyes, backward-pointing teeth, and non-retractile claws for gripping slippery fish.
distinguishing_characteristics: Flattened elongated skull with eyes placed unusually forward and high
Claws are non-retractile, remaining extended to grip slippery aquatic prey
Sharp backward-pointing premolars tailored for gripping fish
Reddish-brown crown with silver-frosted underside
geographic_range: Malay Peninsula, Borneo, and Sumatra
diet: Fish, frogs, freshwater crustaceans, and rodents
behavior: Semiaquatic hunter; dives into river banks; critically threatened by drainage.
image_attribution: Photo: Jim Sanderson / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)

conservation_title: Near Threatened (Smallest wild cat alongside black-footed cat)
description: Rivals the black-footed cat for the title of the world's smallest feline, weighing a mere 0.9 to 1.6 kg. Native to India, Sri Lanka, and Nepal, it features reddish rust-colored spots across its coat.
distinguishing_characteristics: World's smallest wild cat (0.9-1.6 kg)
Rust-colored reddish-brown oval spots over greyish-fawn coat
Huge, piercing rounded eyes relative to face size
Remarkable agility leaping between tree branches despite diminutive stature
geographic_range: India, Sri Lanka, and terrestrial foothills of Nepal
diet: Small rodents, tree frogs, geckos, and large crickets
behavior: Nocturnal and arboreal; extremely agile; elusive predator.
image_attribution: Photo: Davidvraju / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

description: The world's most widespread felid, living in companionship with humanity for over 9,500 years. Descended from the African wildcat, it displays hundreds of coat variations, colors, and breeds.
distinguishing_characteristics: Immense coat diversity (tabby, solid, calico, colorpoint, longhair)
Slit pupils providing high dynamic range vision in shifting light
Righting reflex enabled by flexible spine with 30 vertebrae
Expressive vocalizations adapted specifically for human communication
size_and_weight: Head-body: 46-51 cm; Weight: 3.5-5.5 kg (large breeds up to 11 kg)
geographic_range: Global distribution across human settlements on every continent
diet: Commercial feline diet or small rodents, birds, and insects
behavior: Crepuscular; social flexibility; territorial scent marking.
image_attribution: Photo: Karin Langner-Bahmann, upload von Martin Bahmann / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)

similar_species.differentiator: European wildcats have thicker club-ended blunt tails with crisp black rings and broader jaws.
African wildcats have reddish-orange backs to their ears and slightly longer legs with an upright stance.

description: Inhabits broadleaf and mixed forests across Europe. Characterized by its dense grey-brown coat, broad skull, and a bushy, club-shaped tail with crisp black rings and a blunt black tip.
distinguishing_characteristics: Thick, blunt-ended cylindrical tail with 3-5 distinct black rings
Muted grey-brown coat without white mittens or patches
Significantly wider skull and brain volume than domestic cats
Secretive woodland habit avoiding human settlements
geographic_range: Central, Western, and Southern Europe, Caucasus, and Scottish Highlands
diet: Small rodents (voles, mice) and European rabbits
behavior: Nocturnal and solitary; threatened by hybridization with feral domestic cats.
image_attribution: Photo: Lviatour / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)

similar_species.differentiator: Domestic tabbies have pointed, tapering tails, thinner coats, and often white markings.

description: The biological direct ancestor of all domestic cats. Native to Africa, the Arabian Peninsula, and the Middle East, it is distinguished by rich reddish-ochre coloring on the back of its ears.
distinguishing_characteristics: Conspicuous reddish-ochre color on the back of both ears
Tapering tail with 2-3 dark rings and a black tip
Longer legs giving an upright, dignified standing and sitting posture
Sandy-buff camouflage matching arid savannas
geographic_range: Throughout Africa except central rainforests, Arabian Peninsula, Middle East
diet: Rodents, birds, small reptiles, and scorpions
behavior: Nocturnal and solitary; acute hearing and sudden pounces.
image_attribution: Photo: Bernard DUPONT from FRANCE / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)

description: A large, long-legged member of the genus Felis inhabiting wetlands and reed beds from Egypt across South Asia to southern China. Has small black ear tufts and an unspotted sandy coat.
distinguishing_characteristics: Small black hair tufts (~1.5 cm) on the tips of the ears
Long legs and relatively short tail (roughly one-third of body length)
Uniform sandy-grey to yellowish-brown unspotted coat in adults
High affinity for riverine reed beds and swamp edges
geographic_range: Nile Delta, Middle East, Central Asia, Indian Subcontinent, Southeast Asia
diet: Rodents, waterbirds, hares, frogs, and fish
behavior: Diurnal and crepuscular; stalks along water channels; jumps to catch flushed birds.
image_attribution: Photo: L. Shyamal / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)

similar_species.differentiator: Caracals are larger, deeper reddish in color, with much longer (up to 5 cm) ear tufts.

description: The only true desert-specialist felid, inhabiting hyper-arid dune expanses of the Sahara and Arabian deserts. Its paw pads are thickly carpeted with fur to prevent heat burns and leave zero tracks.
distinguishing_characteristics: Paws densely covered in thick dark fur, leaving no discernible tracks in loose sand
Broad flat head with large, wide-set triangular ears detecting underground sound
Sandy-buff coloration providing total camouflage among desert dunes
Can survive indefinitely without open drinking water, deriving moisture from prey
geographic_range: Sahara Desert of North Africa, Arabian Peninsula, Karakum and Kyzylkum deserts
diet: Desert rodents (gerbils, spiny mice), desert lizards, vipers, and insects
behavior: Nocturnal desert specialist; rests in excavated burrows by day; crouched low gait.
image_attribution: Photo: Payman sazesh / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)

conservation_title: Vulnerable (The most lethal feline hunter on Earth)
description: Africa's smallest wild cat and biologically the world's deadliest feline with an unprecedented 60% hunting success rate. Makes a kill every 50 minutes throughout the night to sustain its high metabolism.
distinguishing_characteristics: Soles of paws and pads are entirely pitch black
Tawny coat densely patterned with bold black spots and distinct neck rings
World's highest feline hunting success rate (60%)
Consumes 250 g of meat every night (one-sixth of its total body mass)
geographic_range: Arid zones of Southern Africa (South Africa, Namibia, Botswana)
diet: Small mammals (elephant shrews, mice), small ground birds, and insects
behavior: Nocturnal sprinter and stalker; walks up to 20 km in a single night searching burrows.
image_attribution: Photo: Patrick Ch. Apfeld, derivative editing by Poke2001 / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 3.0)

description: The only cat species endemic entirely to China, restricted to the northeastern edge of the Tibetan Plateau. Has dense sandy-grey fur, small ear tufts, and a ringed tail with a dark tip.
distinguishing_characteristics: Endemic strictly to the high-elevation Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau (2,800-4,100 m)
Thick sandy-grey winter coat with faint horizontal stripes
Small dark-red ear tufts (~2 cm)
Specialized predator of plateau zokors and pikas
geographic_range: Northeastern Tibetan Plateau in Qinghai and Sichuan, China
diet: Plateau zokors (subterranean rodents), pikas, and birds
behavior: Nocturnal and crepuscular; listens at zokor burrow mounds before excavating.
